emergency-board-up-after-fire/dish.intro: Emergency board up after fire in DISH can be needed when a damaged opening must be protected while the owner is away. We will confirm the authorized work, evaluate the remaining assembly and install the temporary coverage included in the plan.

sections.title: Emergency board up after fire when the owner is away
sections.text: We will confirm the openings authorized for work and the available property access before installation. Existing photographs can help identify the request, but the current surrounding condition still needs evaluation. An opening that has changed since the photos were taken may require a different approach.

sections.title: Evaluate the attachment area on arrival
sections.text: We will inspect accessible frames and adjoining construction for conditions affecting temporary coverage. Weak or unstable material may need another provider first. The work will describe the opening actually secured rather than imply that all exterior damage has been addressed.

sections.title: Preserve the authorized repair access
sections.text: We will account for entry needed by inspectors or restoration providers. Temporary coverage is not a permanent door or window replacement and does not establish occupancy safety. Any relevant exposure outside the requested opening will remain identified separately.

sections.title: Provide a record the owner can review remotely
sections.text: We will document completed coverage and the observed limitations affecting the next step. Later demolition or frame repair may change the supporting area and require review. The record will distinguish the installation performed from permanent repairs still to be arranged.

emergency-board-up-after-fire/dish.estimate: The estimate will distinguish initial installation from later return work. Share the contact coordinating property access and any scheduled inspection so the temporary arrangement supports the known visits.
checklist: Identify the authorized decision contact.
Label photographs by room or side of the property.
Share current entry restrictions and planned visits.

crawl-space-sewage-cleanup/dish.intro: Crawl space sewage cleanup in DISH can be needed after an initial pumping visit leaves residue and affected material beneath the property. We will review what that visit actually covered and complete the authorized physical treatment that remains.

sections.title: Crawl space sewage cleanup in DISH after pumping alone
sections.text: The earlier record may show water collection without describing disposal or surface cleaning. We will identify current accessible liquid and material conditions. Additional extraction will be proposed where necessary, while completed work will remain distinguishable from tasks that were never documented.

sections.title: Remove remaining contamination from the assembly
sections.text: Material designated for disposal will be taken out through the agreed handling route. Retained accessible surfaces will be cleaned to address soil and residue, followed by any appropriate disinfection specified in the plan. Spraying over debris will not be presented as a substitute for the removal and cleaning the surface requires.

sections.title: Document the difference between pumping and restoration
sections.text: We will evaluate moisture and explain the drying needed after treatment. The progress account will identify each completed stage and any area that remained inaccessible. The owner and reconstruction provider can then understand the actual remaining task rather than rely on a broad statement that the crawl space was already cleaned.

crawl-space-sewage-cleanup/dish.estimate: The estimate will focus on the current physical condition and distinguish new work from the earlier collection service. Share invoices, photographs and drain-repair notes so known history and missing information remain clear.
checklist: Identify the areas reached during the first pumping visit.
Share disposal or cleaning records if they exist.
Tell us which components are scheduled for reconstruction.
